lines.en: : Now? But what if he’s busy?
: Then I’ll make him not busy. I’m rich. I can do that.
: Wow! Being rich sounds very fun. And there’s no one more deserving of that than you, Touka.
: Oh, Yasu — you flatter me. Please hold on for one moment.
: Hello?
: Good evening, Sensei. How are-
: What even is evening?
: I’m sorry?

: When does it start? When does it end? It’s not afternoon. It’s not night. And doesn’t afternoon eventually become night? So what room does that leave for evening to exist? Does it even exist at all?
: Um...I...I haven’t really thought about...that before.
: Yeah. That’s why I’m a visionary and you’re not.
: I don’t think you’re a visionary, just that you have visions. Which actually allows me to segue into the reason for my call!
: Are you busy right now? I need your help turning Yasu back into Yasu.
: What is she right now?
: Yasu, of course.
: Great. Then my job here is done.
: You will obey me or I will strip you of the apartment I gifted to you.
: Go ahead. I barely use that place anyway.
: I’ll let you grope one of my breasts for ten seconds.
: Sorry, where are we meeting?
: Is such a lascivious gesture truly worth more to you than free shelter?
: Where. Are. We-
: The cathedral! We’re about to head over now. That won’t be a problem, will it?
: Not for you. You don’t need to run there with an erection.
: Splendid! See you soon, then!
I hang up the phone and immediately begin to make my way over to the seedy area of Kumon-mi where Yasu’s church is located.
The soundtrack then immediately changes upon my arrival because joy does not exist here and because I remember why I was summoned in the first place.
To make a girl feel more like a girl like a girl to make her feel girl to make it.
I should probably go dooooooo that.
: Hello, Sensei! Thank you for returning to these hallowed halls — the chamber in which lambs aren’t sent to slaughter, but laughter! Haha! It’s a joke!
: Hi. I don’t get it.
: Just humor her, please. But yes, thank you for coming.
: No problem. Do I get my reward now or later?
: Hm? What reward?
: You fucking-
: NO SWEARING IN CHURCH!!!!!
: Today, we’re going to play a game! It’s one I used to play with the rabbits — and the idea is to find out what color your light is.
: All you have to do is answer a series of questions as truthfully as you can so I can consult with the Book of Colors about what color you are! It’s another joke! Hahah!
: Correct me if I’m wrong here, but didn’t you say something about Yasu not being Yasu when we were on the phone? Because she seems very Yasu to me right now.
: I assure you this is more surprising to me than it is to you. I’ve been with her all day and it wasn’t until you arrived that she started acting...normal again.
: HehhehehahahahahahahAHAHA! You knew it would work, Touka! You’re so smart and wonderful! And Sensei! You are so bright. It’s like you haven’t grown a day!
: Uhh...what?
: Just be nice and play along. She’s undergone a long and arduous medicinal journey as of late and I see this as giving her a chance to play around in the sandbox for an hour or two.
: Okay...but if things go south, you can’t blame me for it. Places like this don’t really mix with the masses of strange misshapen gods appearing to me on a weekly basis now.
: The what?
: Remember! Honestly and truthfully! Just think about what Wormwood says — lie about your light and you’ll lie alone at night! Do both of you understand?
: Poor Niki. I wonder what will happen to her.
: Hopefully nothing as dramatic as you. Please continue, Yasu.
: Hahahehehah! Okay! This is going to be so much fun!
: Question one! What would you do with three plates of squid?
: Um...in what context, may I ask?
: Are the squid...prepared? Are they alive?
: They are whatever you want them to be! There is no right or wrong answer, Touka! Just believe in yourself and say whatever it is you want to say! It’s a game, remember?
: I...suppose that is true. But if I could have a moment to ponder over the potential answers, I-
: Three plates of squid. Three plates of squid. What would you do with three plates of squid?
: As I was saying, I’m attempting to formulate an answer. But it requires more than-
: Would you eat ‘em all up? Cut ‘em up nice? Dice ‘em in pieces and feed ‘em to mice?
: Can mice even-
: Three plates of squid. Three plates of squid. Death isn’t real and joy they forbid.
: Is this...some sort of strange nursery rhyme they tell to commoners?
: I...don’t know. I just...wanted to say all of that for...some reason.
: Your answer has been recorded! Touka?
: I would distribute them amongst the needy.
: Yay! Now your answer has been recorded!
: Question two — what is love?
: The most beautiful thing in the world — shared traditionally between a man and woman, but also between all sorts of other people as I have recently learned. Which I think is wonderful.
: Blind...
: Typical. My answer was better.
: Your answers have been recorded!
: Question three — which coffee machine is the arch nemesis of the Hario v60?
: Now what does that even-
: The Kalita Wave. Keep going.
: What is a Kalita Wave? What is a Hario v60? How did you come up with an answer so quickly and why does Yasu’s color game involve questions about coffee machines?
: I don’t know...but I know the answers.
: Ahem. There are no right or wrong answers, Sensei. Even Yasu says-
: ANSWER THE QUESTION, TOUKA!
: It’s important that we don’t keep the Book of Colors waiting.
: I...concur with Sensei’s assessment that the “Kalita Wave” is the arch nemesis of the-
: Question four — who said there is nothing to fear but fear itself?
: Franklin Delano Roosevelt! I know this one! Ha! That means there are right and wrong answers! I’ve been deceived!
: ...yeah. My answer is the same.
: Your answers have been recorded! Question five — breathing the right way? How to do? How many? Only two!
: That one doesn’t even make any sense! I hate this game! How could someone possibly-
: You know...

: Perhaps there...is some sort of link between the two of you. Because, whether it be conscious or not, you’re hardly even hesitating with these. And Yasu seems far more pleased with your answers than mine.
: He’s doing an excellent job, I think! But it’s not the answers themselves that matter most, dearest Touka! It’s the confidence with which one says them.
: Then I am going to say 19. That way, there is a 50%% chance that my answer is closer if Sensei is wrong. Which I know is possible because of FDR.
: Your answer has been recorded. There are only six thousand, nine hundred, seventy-four questions to go until we figure out what color your light is.
: Yasu...can you show me that clipboard?
: Do you not trust me, Sensei?...
: It’s less that I don’t trust you and more that I just...want to know why the answers to all of these are immediately coming to me.
: Perhaps you played this same sort of game when you were younger? It’s true that you can’t recall much about your past, isn’t it?
: Yeah...maybe. This wouldn’t be the first time Yasu just...knew things about my past for some reason. Which is why I want to see what she’s holding.
: That’s not how the game works, unfortunately. I ask the questions. You answer them. Then we find out what color your light is together.

: If you see the questions beforehand, you’ll have time to think of answers. If you have time to think of answers, you won’t answer honestly. Do you want to be red? Because it sounds like you want to be red.
: Is there a problem with red, Yasu?
: Yes! Red is bad! Those who are coated in the prism’s blood shall not find peace in their departure from this plane! Have you not been listening to me?! I say it all the time!
: Yasu...please calm down. Remember what we talked about earlier, okay? You can say whatever you like here, but getting carried away can still be dangerous. And you don’t want to upset Sensei.
: Hooooohhhh......
: Gooooood...
: In...then out....
: Just like that...
: Um...maybe...not like that.
: Hah...haah...hah!...
: Why are the rabbits here, Yasu? Which ones...are they?
: Hah...hah...Penemue...and...Etinsib Ziwa...
: I haven’t met that one before, have I?
: You’ve been keeping track of their names?
: I’m weirdly good at remembering stuff like that.
: That’s strange because you’re utterly horrible at remembering effectively everything else.
: Hah...hah...no...you have not met...
: At least...not the you...currently inhabiting...you....
: But he was looking forward to this day...for he knew someone that you knew...but he dare not speak their name.
: Well, I guess that all but confirms that connection I mentioned moments ago.
: Can you speak their name, Yasu?

: I’m afraid I don’t know it. I am but a broken-winged fledgling compared to the rabbits and their aeons worth of knowledge. All I can do is deliver the messages small enough to fit in the clutches of my intangible talons.
: But even if I did know...I’m not sure I could tell you.
: It’s not part of the game.
: And will we be getting back to this “game” any time soon? Because it feels as if we’ve gotten rather sidetracked between the yelling and...breathing.
: Yes! Yes...you’re right. That’s...why we’re here. I must stay...focused on the task at hand and...maintain this...newly discovered...free will...
: Question...
: Question six...
: If the world were to start anew...and you could only take one soul with you...
: Who would it be?...
: This is significantly more bleak than the rest of your questions thus far. Is such an answer really necessary to decipher our color?
: This question is special...it provides a fast track to a somewhat accurate result for those who don’t mind skipping the rest of the quiz.
: Oh, excellent. I can’t imagine either one of us wants to stick around for thousands more of these.
: I suppose I’ll just say my mother. I care deeply for her and still have much left to learn.
: Wow, thanks.
: What? You didn’t really think I’d choose you, did you?
: Good luck starting civilization all over with your mom. At least you and I could reproduce.
: Oh my.
: I’ll take Ami. I owe it to her.
: Even after bringing up reproduction?!
: Fine, I’ll just copy your answer and take your mom too then.
: Aaaah! I hate this stupid game! No offense, Yasu! It’s been very fun and I hope you were able to effectively communicate with your god again!
: Thank you, Touka. I’m sorry if you hated it. I did have a lot of fun, though! But unfortunately, I didn’t hear as much as I wanted to...
: Either way! Give me a minute to look up your results in the Book of Colors!
: Has she ever brought up this “Book of Colors” thing to you before?
: Unlike you, I have quite a difficult time keeping track of all of this spiritual nonsense. It’s possible she has, I assume. But it’s not as if I specifically remember it.
: What do you think is in there?
: Over six thousand more personality quiz questions, at the very least.
: Seriously, though. Aren’t you at least a little interested?
: Not as much as you, it seems. But I’m not the one with deep-seated memories of any of this. If they really are just memories and you can’t apparently hear things too.
: I used to.
: Oh, fantastic.
: Not so much anymore, though.
: Oh, fantastic. But for real this time.
: I’m just saying...maybe Yasu isn’t as crazy as everyone makes her out to be? Maybe we should let her ramble on and...be mean if she wants to. Maybe we’ll learn something?

: That was my intention! That’s why I called you here! There’s just something deeply unsettling to me whenever I see that adorably pathetic girl begin to slip away and be replaced by...some kind of demon!
: I’m a demon like 99%% of the time and you still willingly talk to me.
: Yes, but you don’t giggle when I brush your hair or ask to sleep in my bed during thunderstorms.
: I’m naturally protective of Yasu. Like an actual mother. Not the fetishistic type you see me as. I shan’t be blamed for becoming uncomfortable watching the poor girl get aroused by deep breathing.
: In her defense, you did make it sound kind of sexual.
: Not purposely! Why does everything with you always have to have some sort of inappropriate undertone?!

: That’s not purposeful either. It’s just the way I think. And Yasu clearly has her own distinctive way of thinking too. So don’t you think it might be beneficial to just...let her go off and see what happens?
: Perhaps you’re right...
: I just worry that some of her beliefs are a bit too...unconventional to justify indulging her. But I suppose that this is the safest sort of environment we can cultivate for her at the end of the-
: I have received your results from the Book of Colors...
: I have received your results from the Book of Colors!
: And great news! You’re not red! You can still ascend! There’s still hope left for both of you!
: H...Hooraaaay! Is there...anything we must do next? Or is the game just...over now?
: There is one more thing! But I don’t want to make you stay here if you are bored and tired of my existence. Both of you are free to leave me here to rot instead if that is what you prefer!
: No, Yasu. We will not leave you here to rot. Just tell us what the next step is and we’ll happily oblige.
: The next step is to make sure your color doesn’t change!
: In this world of infinite possibilities, it is easier than ever to be tainted by misdeeds and temptation! But if you take a vow of loyalty, you can prevent their untimely onset!
: Hah. Okay. I, Touka Tsukioka, hereby swear to remain loyal to-
: Not here, Touka! No! We have to go somewhere else!
: Y...Yasu. We need to remain here. Exercising your “free will” outside of this place is-
: It is here, Touka! It is!
: Just follow me! I’ll show you! It’s amazing! The most amazing thing you’ll ever see!
: O-Oh! Okay. I...I suppose we’re...relocating then, Sensei. A-After you.
: You’re not scared, are you?
: Me? Scared?! Ha! No! Nuh-uh! I just...think that you should go first since you’re the tallest.
: We’ll all go together! Come on, come on, come on!
